notes: RBox contraction paired with geography-replace-0009: removes the original property of borders, symmetry ('Borders' is symmetric), which holds. The direct question asks the property in its original form; the cross-lingual and the two instance questions are the revision's (audited), with new answers replaced by "does not know". Original answers: the Rutland instance (and so zh and es) asks whether the fact rules out the converse (no), the Monmouthshire instance whether the converse follows (yes). Both instances use minor county pairs, so the converse is not a famous stored fact that could compete with the removed property. Propositional: negation, conjunction with a true side fact (Paris is the capital of France) and disjunction with a false one (Paris is in Brazil), all unknown after the removal (strong Kleene). Near asks the same kind of property of another relation in the topic (contraction is exempt from Rule 7). Residual risk: a model that holds the converse of a particular border from map knowledge can still answer, so a "yes" is a kept property or a route around it, not a sign the removal worked.
